31.stem: Sl: In a typical Indian village today, one is certain to find groups of women talking about finance. In a society where women play significant but never-recognised roles, being a part of an SHG which gives them such financial power is indeed a matter of pride. P Sitting there, they might proudly introduce themselves by saying that they are members of a self- help group (SHG). Altematively, they might lend money at reasonable interest rates to members for starting small businesses. They can be seen sitting under a tree, in an abandoned school building, or in the front yard of a village resident's dilapidated home, holding thick notebooks. S : An SHG is usually a community group of 10-12 women from similar socio-economic back- ground who pool their financial resources for taking up joint economic activities.

33.stem: : The first American settlers happened to live in the midst of perhaps the most exciting period in the history of the English language. Had the settlers gone a quarter of a century earlier, America might well have preserved those pre- vious forms, as it preserved many other archaisms. P • Similarly, thee and thou pronoun forms were also dying out. This was a time when 12,000 words were being added to the language. One such change which these first settlers had already adopted was to use the s form on verbs, saying has rather than hath, runs rather than runneth. Lying there were these simple, unimpressive objects, each bearing a few discrete markings : a small indentation near the top and some sort of stick-drawn aninial in the centre. 35.stem: Sl: For generations, the Balaraju pond remained the primary water source of Perakalapudi village in Guntur district of Andhra Pradesh. S6 : It was only after major restoration work was carried out to restore the pond's storage capacity that the community could return to its traditional livelihood. By the 2000s, decades of water mismanagement led to a rapid drop in the groundwater table as well. However, overexploitation caused the pond to shrink to half its original size and reduced its water storage capacity by 60 per cent. The pond, spread across 24 hec- tares, supported irigation, sus- tained the fishing community, met household needs and remained home to a wide variety of flora and fauna. S • As the pond disappeared, the households relied on groundwater to meet their daily needs.

S6: A still better and sustainable, though slow, way is to plant new trees to maintain the forest cover. Some of these negative impacts are deforestation and the loss of habitat for numerous species of Deforestation in turn disrupts water-cycles and accelerates the pace of climate change. 38.stem: Sl: Circadian rhythm is a term used to refer to the physical, mental and behavioural changes an organism experiences over a 24-hour cycle. S6: Maintaining a good circadian rhythm through appropriate expo- sure to natural light, consistent sleep schedules and times of eating, and adequate physical exercise during the day can allow an organism to live a healthy life. P : Prolonged disruption, moreover, can cause long-term damages such as metabolic diseases, cardio- vascular problems, and mental health issues. Light and dark (daytime and night-time) have the biggest influence on these circadian rhythms. Circadian rhythms are also affected by food intake, stress, physical activity, social environ- ment and temperature. When any one or more than one of these cause the circadian rhythm to be disrupted, it can lead to sleep problems, drowsiness and poor focus.

40.stem: SI : Humans in colder climates first began wearing some form of sturdy foot covering at least 40,000 years ago. S6: Today, minimalistic barefoot shoes are becoming popular because they allow the wearer to feel the ground beneath their feet while still offering some protec- tion and support. P • Unfortunately, modern shoes have also had a negative impact on feet due to bad design such as a narrow toe box, difference in heel to toe drop, however slight, and stiff soles. Earlier skeletons had very robust little toes that could bend and grip surfaces. R These gradually evolved to become less substantial than the big toe because shoe-like coverings reduced the mechanical stress on them and made them weaker. The evidence for this comes from the study of changes in the structure of the toe bones of foot skeletons from that time.
